options.content: Pilots: Live now · Traffic · New pilots · Origins · Records · Routes · Aircraft · Military | ATC: Overview · Retention · Hours · Positions · Ranks | Events: **Monday events** | Management: Health All times are UTC. Figures cover VATPAC airspace.

panels.title: Monday event attendance (0700-1200Z)
panels.description: Pilots and controllers present between 0700 and 1200 UTC on each Monday.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT win_start AS time, pilot_cids AS "Pilots", controller_cids AS "Controllers"
FROM monday_attendance
WHERE win_start BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
ORDER BY win_start

panels.title: Share of YMML-YSSY airborne time flown by local pilots (Mondays 0700-1200Z)
panels.description: Weekly share of Melbourne-Sydney airborne time flown by home-region pilots, Mondays 0700 to 1200 UTC.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT (date_trunc('week', f.end_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS time,
       round(100.0 * COALESCE(sum(f.airborne_minutes) FILTER (WHERE f.pilot_is_local), 0)
             / NULLIF(sum(f.airborne_minutes), 0), 1) AS "Local pilots (%)"
FROM flight_ext f
WHERE f.end_time BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  AND extract(isodow FROM f.end_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') = 1
  AND (f.end_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::time >= time '07:00'
  AND (f.end_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::time < time '12:00'
  AND ((f.departure = 'YMML' AND f.arrival = 'YSSY') OR (f.departure = 'YSSY' AND f.arrival = 'YMML'))
  AND f.airborne_minutes > 0
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Aircraft airborne during the Monday event window, each Monday (0700-1200Z)
panels.description: Question G1 (issue 324). Definition: for each Monday (UTC) in the last 5 years that has any, the number of distinct finished flights that were connected at some moment between 0700 and 1200 UTC and had airborne time above 0 (groundspeed of 60 kt or more at some point, as on the weekday and weekend charts). A flight that overlaps the window by even one minute counts once, however long it spans it. The flight summary stores when a flight started and ended and its total airborne minutes, not when it was airborne, so a flight that took off and landed outside the window but stayed connected into it is counted: the bars are an upper bound of the aircraft actually in the air during the window. Imported v1 flights are included (no altitude is needed). A flight counts about 8 hours after its last position, so the latest Monday fills in during that evening. Times are UTC.

targets.rawSql:
-- Each flight is expanded to the UTC days it touches; only Mondays are kept, so the query reads the flights once
SELECT to_char(m.monday, 'DD-MM-YYYY') AS "Monday (UTC)",
       count(DISTINCT f.session_id) AS "Aircraft airborne"
FROM flight f
CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(date_trunc('day', f.start_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'),
                                   date_trunc('day', f.end_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'), interval '1 day') AS d(day)
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT d.day::date AS monday,
                           (d.day::date + time '07:00') AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS win_start,
                           (d.day::date + time '12:00') AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS win_end) m
WHERE f.airborne_minutes > 0
  AND f.end_time >= ($__timeFrom())::timestamptz
  AND f.start_time <= ($__timeTo())::timestamptz
  AND extract(isodow FROM d.day) = 1
  AND f.start_time < m.win_end
  AND f.end_time > m.win_start
  AND m.win_start BETWEEN ($__timeFrom())::timestamptz AND ($__timeTo())::timestamptz
GROUP BY m.monday
ORDER BY m.monday
